turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I've got a sunny balcony and I want to grow something I can actually eat.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Lovely. Herbs, cherry tomatoes and salad greens all do well in pots. Which of those would you use the most?

contexts.pending: herbs, cherry tomatoes or salad greens
think_reask: So, which would you use most, herbs, tomatoes or salad greens?
Okay, time's up. What do you want on your balcony first?
Have you picked yet, herbs, cherry tomatoes or greens?
welcome_back: Welcome back! We were planning your balcony garden. Herbs, tomatoes or greens?
Hi again. You were choosing what to grow on your sunny balcony.
There you are. Any thoughts on what to plant first?

endings.user: Herbs, for sure. I'm always buying basil.
endings.moshi: Then start with basil, parsley and mint. Keep the mint in its own pot, it spreads like crazy.

endings.user: Cherry tomatoes. My kids would love picking them.
endings.moshi: Great choice. Get a big pot, a stake for support, and water them every day when it's hot.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: There's a bare patch in my back garden, maybe two meters wide, and it gets shade most of the day.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Shade is tricky but doable. Do you want flowers there, or something low-maintenance like ferns and ground cover?

contexts.pending: flowers or low-maintenance ferns for shady patch
think_reask: So, for that shady patch, flowers or something low-maintenance?
Alright, have you decided what kind of look you want for the shady spot?
welcome_back: Welcome back. We were talking about your shady patch. Flowers or ferns?
Good to have you back. Did you decide what to put in that bare spot?

endings.user: Some flowers would be nice, a bit of color.
endings.moshi: Try hostas, foxgloves and impatiens. They're happy in shade and still bring some color.

endings.user: Low-maintenance. I really don't have time.
endings.moshi: Then ferns and some ivy or periwinkle as ground cover. Once settled, they mostly look after themselves.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: We're building raised beds this weekend. Wood or metal?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Wood looks natural and is cheaper, metal lasts longer and warms up faster in spring. What matters more to you, budget or durability?

think_reask: So, budget or durability? Wood or metal beds?
Okay, back to the raised beds. Have you decided on wood or metal?
welcome_back: Welcome back! We were picking material for your raised beds.
Hey, you're back. Still weighing up wood against metal?

endings.user: Budget, so let's go with wood.
endings.moshi: Good. Use untreated larch or cedar if you can, they resist rot without any chemicals.

endings.user: Metal. I don't want to rebuild them in five years.
endings.moshi: Sensible. Line the bottom with cardboard before you fill them, it smothers the weeds.

turns.speaker: friend

turns.speaker: friend

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: How often should I water my houseplants?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Most like to dry out a bit between waterings. Push a finger into the soil, and if the top few centimeters are dry, it's time.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: So not on a fixed schedule?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Not really. In winter they need much less, and in summer they might need it twice a week.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I have a cactus and a / what's it called, a peace lily.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Those are opposites. Water the cactus maybe once a month, and the peace lily when its leaves start to droop a little.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Oh, it droops? I thought that meant it was dying.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: It's just being dramatic. Give it a good drink and it usually perks up within a few hours.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: When should I plant tulip bulbs?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: In autumn, once the soil has cooled down. Late October to November is usually ideal.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: How deep do they go?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: About three times the height of the bulb, so roughly fifteen to twenty centimeters, pointy end up.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And can I put them in pots? I was hoping to / put a few by the front door.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Yes, tulips look great in pots. Pack them closely together and make sure the pot drains well.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Do they come back every year?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Some do, but many fade after the first year. Lots of people just plant fresh ones each autumn.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I want to start composting but I live in a flat. Is that even possible?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: It is. A small worm bin or a bokashi bucket can live under your sink and won't smell if you look after it.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Worms in my kitchen? My partner would / probably move out.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Then bokashi might be easier. It's a sealed bucket where you add scraps and a sprinkle of bran, no worms involved.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What do I do with it when it's full?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Bury it in soil, a large planter or a community garden bed. After a few weeks it turns into rich compost.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: There's a community garden two streets over actually.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Perfect, ask them. Most community gardens are happy to take it.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My lawn has yellow patches all over. What's going on?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Common causes are dry weather, dog pee or grubs in the soil. Do you have a dog?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Yeah, a big one.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That's likely it then. Watering the spot right after the dog goes can dilute it and stop the burn.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I can't follow him around with a watering can all day.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Fair. You could train him to use one corner of the garden, or reseed the patches in spring.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Reseeding sounds easier. Do I just / throw seeds on top?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Rake the patch first to loosen the soil, then sprinkle the seed and keep it moist for two weeks.
